Hi Aarti — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short answer: yes, we can keep span-highlighting and the model-ensemble on ByteBundle, but there are trade-offs and a small one-time configuration fee for reserved KV cache capacity to avoid regressions on latency.

What I'm sending now: 1) a concise proposal (attached) with pricing delta and options, 2) a feature-compatibility matrix that shows behavior differences when moved from Throughput Plus -> ByteBundle. See the attachments: aurora_bytebundle_proposal_v1.pdf and feature-compatibility-matrix.csv.

High-level notes:
- Capabilities: span-highlighting and ensemble will function identically from an output-quality perspective.
- Latency: without reserved KV cache the p95 token latency may increase ~20-40% under spiky load; reserved KV cache keeps p95 within 10% of your current SLA.
- Pricing: two paths — (A) ByteBundle + one-time config fee ($8k) + small monthly KV reserve ($1,200/mo) or (B) ByteBundle + transient burst credits (pay-as-you-go token surge) (likely cheaper if your spikes are rare).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben (cc'd) to confirm the platform-side config timeline.
2) If acceptable, we draft an amendment to the Quote (I'll attach redline-ready language).
3) Quick pilot run (7 days) with reserved KV at 50% of current working set to validate latency.

Happy to jump on 30m this week with procurement + your engineering lead to go over numbers.

Cheers,

Hi Aarti — quick technical note from engineering: the ensemble path requires an extra KV set per request to maintain synchronous voting across model variants. On Throughput Plus that's cached aggressively; on ByteBundle we rely on a smaller shared cache which is where the p95 delta comes from under bursty traffic.

Specific recommendations:
- For clinical flows (latency-sensitive), we recommend reserving a dedicated KV pool equal to ~50-60% of today's working set to hit p95 targets. That is the config fee + monthly reservation Mina called out.
- If Aurora wants to avoid the reservation fee, we can set up auto-burst credits with throttles and a second-tier fallback model to preserve availability but you'll see increased inference cost when spikes occur.

I can run a short simulation against a sample trace if you can share a typical 24-hr spike window (anonymized). If you prefer, we can do the 7-day pilot Mina suggested and measure tail latency and cost.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
